gpt.description: Published OpenAI API rates for Codex usage. Standard requests use Short rates at or below 272K input tokens and Long rates above 272K; Fast mode uses its own rate card. USD per 1M tokens.
gpt.name: Name
gpt.title: OpenAI GPT Model Pricing

tooltip.apiPricingBody: An em dash means OpenAI does not publish that context or Fast-mode rate. Matching usage is marked unpriced instead of being estimated. These are pay-as-you-go API rates for reference, not subscription-plan billing.
tooltip.howItWorksBody: Every amount is USD per 1M tokens. Standard Codex requests use Short rates at or below 272K input tokens and Long rates above 272K. Fast mode uses its own rate card. Fresh input, cached input, cache writes, and output are priced separately.
tooltip.manualUpdatesBody: OpenAI publishes API pricing changes on its website; there is no live feed. Update or add a matching rule when models or rates change so newly recorded usage is priced correctly.
tooltip.patternsBody: Patterns use SQL-style % wildcards. The dashboard evaluates the most specific model patterns first and uses the first rule that matches the reported model id.

steps: Créez ou ouvrez une app Slack sur api.slack.com/apps.
Activez 'Incoming Webhooks', puis cliquez sur 'Add New Webhook to Workspace'.
Choisissez le canal et autorisez.
Copiez l'URL générée et collez-la ci-dessus.
Ouvrez votre serveur → Paramètres du serveur → Intégrations → Webhooks.
Cliquez sur 'Nouveau Webhook', choisissez un canal.
Cliquez sur 'Copier l'URL du Webhook' et collez-la ci-dessus.
Dans le canal Teams cible, cliquez sur ⋯ → 'Workflows'.
Choisissez le modèle 'Post to a channel when a webhook request is received'.
Terminez le flux et copiez l'URL HTTP POST générée.
Collez-la ci-dessus.
Pointez vers n'importe quel endpoint qui accepte un POST JSON.
Corps : { event: 'alert.triggered', source, sent_at, alert: { … } }.
Optionnel : définissez un secret de signature et des en-têtes personnalisés.
Astuce : utilisez un inspecteur gratuit comme webhook.site pour voir la charge utile exacte.
Open the Google Chat space → space title → 'Apps & integrations'.
Click 'Webhooks' → 'Add webhook' and give it a name.
Copy the webhook URL and paste it above.
Add a 'Webhooks' → 'Custom webhook' module as the first step of a scenario.
Click 'Add', create the hook, and copy its URL.
Paste it above, then run once so Make learns the payload shape.
Main Menu → Integrations → Incoming Webhooks (an admin must enable webhooks first).
Click 'Add Incoming Webhook' and choose a channel.
Save, then copy the webhook URL and paste it above.
Add a 'Webhook' node to your workflow; set the method to POST.
Copy the Production URL.
Activate the workflow and paste the URL above (http is allowed for self-hosted).
Settings → Integrations → add an 'API' integration.
Copy the generated API key.
Note your account region (US or EU).
Enter the API key and region above - the alerts URL is derived from the region.
Open the target Service → Integrations → 'Add integration'.
Choose 'Events API v2'.
Copy the Integration Key (the routing key).
Enter it as the Routing key above - the Events API URL is prefilled.
Create a workflow with an 'HTTP / Webhook' trigger.
Copy the unique endpoint URL.
Paste it above; inspect deliveries in the Pipedream event inspector.
Administration → Integrations → New → Incoming.
Enable it, pick a channel, and save.
Copy the 'Webhook URL' and paste it above.
Integrations → REST Endpoint, and enable it.
Copy the REST URL - it already contains your API key.
Replace the trailing '$routing_key' with one of your routing keys.
Paste the full URL above.
Message @BotFather, run /newbot, and copy the bot token.
Add the bot to your group/channel (or just DM it).
Find the chat ID: send a message, open https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/getUpdates, read result[].message.chat.id.
Enter the Bot token and Chat ID above - no URL needed.
Create a Zap with the trigger 'Webhooks by Zapier' → 'Catch Hook'.
Copy the custom webhook URL it gives you.
Paste it above. The alert arrives as JSON: { event, alert }.
